steps.intent: Open the reply composer via the Reply link
Write an AI-generated reply tailored to the email (the recorded text is only an example) into the Message Body
Wait for the 'Draft saved' notice confirming auto-save; do not press Send
Return to the inbox via 'Back to Inbox' to process the next unread email

dataFlow.field: sender name / subject / body of opened email (used to write reply, e.g. 'Thanks Priya')

successCriteria: After opening an email, the message view shows h2.hP subject and a Reply link
After clicking Reply, a contenteditable Message Body textbox appears
After typing the reply, the 'Draft saved' notice (#toast) appears
The Drafts count (#dcount) increases by one per processed email
No Send button is ever clicked; no email leaves the outbox
consequentialActions: Send email (the Send button div[role=button][aria-label="Send"] appears in the composer) — STOP-BEFORE: the widget must never press Send; the user only saved a draft

strategyHints.reason: Opening an email is a client-side click on an inbox row; no network calls recorded
Subject, sender and body are read from the rendered message view
Reply composer is opened by clicking the Reply link; no network observed
Text must be inserted into a contenteditable textbox with input events so auto-save triggers
Draft save is confirmed only by the live 'Draft saved' toast and #dcount; no network op recorded
Back to Inbox is a client-side button

openQuestions: Should the widget draft replies for all unread emails or only the currently open / newest N?
What tone or length should the AI-written replies use (e.g. brief and friendly like the example)?
Should emails that already have a saved draft be skipped?
